title: A living computer uses bacteria to solve a maths puzzle

questions.q: At each junction the program asks whether to use the number 4. Which line takes in input?
questions.explain: RECEIVE ... FROM KEYBOARD on line 3 is the input, while line 2 just sets a value inside the program without asking anyone.

questions.q: The user types skip. What does the program display?
questions.explain: skip is not "use", so the ELSE part displays Skipped and total stays 0, and the last line still runs because it is after END IF.

questions.q: What data type is stored in temperature?
questions.explain: 31.5 has a decimal part, so it is a real number, and it isn't an integer because integers are whole numbers only.

questions.q: One bacterium splits in two again and again. What is the value of bacteria at the end?
questions.explain: Doubling 5 times goes 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and it isn't 10 because the loop multiplies by 2 rather than adding 2.
It displays for 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16, then stops when explorers reaches 32, so it is 5 times and not 4 because the first pass happens at 1.
routes becomes 2, 4, 8 and 16, and only 8 and 16 are more than 4, so it is 2 times and not 3 because 4 > 4 is FALSE.

questions.q: What kind of loop is this?
questions.explain: REPEAT ... UNTIL stops when its condition becomes TRUE, so it is conditional, and it isn't fixed because no number of times is given.

questions.q: The numbers 2 and 8 are picked. Is total = target AND total > 5 TRUE or FALSE?
questions.explain: total is 10, which equals the target and is more than 5, so both sides are TRUE and AND gives TRUE.

questions.q: Is the maze too cold or too hot? Is temperature < 25 OR temperature > 35 TRUE or FALSE?
questions.explain: 30 is not below 25 and not above 35, so both sides are FALSE, and OR needs at least one TRUE side.

questions.q: Checking one route takes 1 minute. There are 8 routes and 4 explorers work in parallel, each checking 2 routes. How long does it take?
questions.explain: Each explorer checks 2 routes at the same time as the others, so it takes 2 minutes, not 8, which is how long one explorer alone would take.

questions.q: Abstraction: which detail does the maze NOT need to solve the puzzle?
options: A use-or-skip choice at each junction
questions.explain: The bacteria's colour changes nothing about which numbers add up to the target, while the target and the choices are the puzzle itself.

questions.q: A program checks the maze temperature is from 20 to 37 degrees. Someone types hot. What kind of test data is that?
questions.explain: hot is not a number at all, so it is exceptional data that the program should reject, not boundary data, which sits right at the edge of the range.

questions.q: Would you trust a living computer made of bacteria to solve a hard problem?
options: Yes, if the answer is checked
No, I'd use a normal computer
questions.explain: Talk about it: bacteria sometimes take a wrong turn, so how could scientists be sure an answer is right?
